$comment: The connector registry — the vocabulary `wired_into` is allowed to use (frontmatter-schema.md
invariant 5: a name that is not here is refused with `unknown_connector`, never silently dropped).
This file is the DATA half. The CODE half is CONNECTOR_REGISTRY in
apps/runner/src/lib/allowlist.ts, and `connectors.test.ts` asserts the two have identical
keys — so `npm run validate:frontmatter` and the running runner can never disagree about
whether an agent is wireable. Adding a row here without adding it there is caught by that
test, not by a confused user at 2am.
Adding a connector deliberately widens what agents in this library can do. It is not a step
you take to unblock one agent. `tools` is the concrete allowlist a run receives; a trailing
`*` is a prefix match, which is how one MCP server exposes a family of tools under one name.

workspace.label: Scratch workspace
workspace.note: Read/write inside the per-run scratch dir only (§3.2). The directory is destroyed after artifact extraction, which is what keeps this connector ordinary.

shell.label: Shell
shell.note: Deliberately separate from `workspace`. Most agents must not have it.

gmail.label: Gmail
gmail.note: Draft and send; send is gated by approval: required.

git.label: Git
git.note: Repo history. Which paths a commit may touch is bounded by the runner (agents/** for schedules, company/** for the brain), not by this grant — ADR-002, ADR-007.

company-brain.label: Company brain
company-brain.note: Read/write company/COMPANY.md + sources. The interview agent's power is a connector rather than an implicit capability so that it shows up in WIRED INTO like everything else (§3.3).
